Strong interaction

Words: 154 Articles: 3
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
The strong interaction is the SU(3)c​ gauge interaction described by Quantum chromodynamics. It couples quarks and gluons through color charge.

Meson-baryon scattering

Words: 135 Articles: 2
Strong interaction OurBigBook.com
Scattering with one meson and one baryon in the initial and final states. The strong interaction conserves electric charge, baryon number, net strangeness, four-momentum, total angular momentum, and parity. Approximate isospin symmetry imposes additional relations among charge-channel amplitudes.

Strangeness selection in pion-proton and kaon-proton resonances

Words: 62
Meson-baryon scattering OurBigBook.com
The π+p channel has baryon number one, strangeness zero and I3​=3/2, matching the ordinary uuu Delta baryon. The K+p channel has strangeness plus one, which no three-light-quark baryon can have because each strange quark contributes minus one. A resonance in that channel would require exotic content such as four quarks and an antiquark; the ordinary low-energy qqq multiplets therefore explain the contrast.

Pion-nucleon octet channels (πN→πN,η8​N,KΛ,KΣ)

Words: 43
Meson-baryon scattering OurBigBook.com
For an initial pion-nucleon state and outgoing meson octet-baryon octet pair, conservation of baryon number and strangeness allows πN, η8​N, KΛ, and KΣ, subject to electric charge and production thresholds. Total isospin is 1/2 or 3/2; the η8​N and KΛ channels contain only 1/2.

Weak interaction

Words: 849 Articles: 18
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
The weak interaction is the short-range chiral interaction mediated by the W and Z bosons. Above the electroweak scale it is part of the unbroken SU(2)L​×U(1)Y​ electroweak gauge theory.

Charged-lepton flavor violation

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Weak interaction OurBigBook.com
Processes that change individual charged-lepton family numbers are absent perturbatively in the minimal massless-neutrino Standard Model. A flavour-misaligned Higgs coupling can permit decays such as h→μτ. Neutrino masses and mixing permit extremely suppressed loop effects, while additional flavour structures can give larger rates.

Dimension-six Higgs Yukawa misalignment (Yh​=Mdiag​/v+v2λ′/Λ2)

Words: 52
Charged-lepton flavor violation OurBigBook.com
An operator (Lˉi​ϕeRj​)(ϕ†ϕ)/Λ2 contains three factors of v+h. Its contribution to the mass matrix is proportional to v3, while its single-Higgs coupling is three times the corresponding mass-over-v contribution. With the normalization −2​λ′/Λ2, the mass-basis coupling is Yh​=Mdiag​/v+v2λ′/Λ2. Nonzero off-diagonal coefficients permit charged-lepton flavour-violating Higgs decays.

Charged current

Words: 535 Articles: 10
Weak interaction OurBigBook.com
The weak charged current couples a W boson to two members of a left-handed electroweak doublet. In the quark mass basis its flavor coefficients are entries of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix.

Orthogonal completion of mixed neutral lepton kinetic terms (nL​=cα​νL​+sα​NL​,nL⊥​=−sα​νL​+cα​NL​)

Words: 70
Charged current OurBigBook.com
If a chiral fermion triplet uses one normalized linear combination of two neutral leptons, adding the perpendicular combination as a gauge singlet completes their canonical kinetic terms. The two combinations are related to the original fields by a real orthogonal matrix. Hence their summed kinetic quadratic form is exactly that of the two original fields, with no mixed terms. The singlet carries the same chirality; no right-handed component is created for a purely left-handed massless neutrino.

Lepton universality (ge​=gμ​=gτ​)

Words: 50
Charged current OurBigBook.com
The Standard Model assigns the same gauge coupling to each lepton generation in the weak charged current. Different decay rates still arise from masses and phase space. Ratios of leptonic pion decay rates cancel the common hadronic decay constant and quark mixing coefficient, isolating universality and helicity suppression. Electromagnetic radiative corrections must be included for precision comparisons to inclusive measured decay rates.

Quark mixing (V=UuL†​UdL​)

Words: 49
Charged current OurBigBook.com
The up-type and down-type fermion mass matrices need different left-handed transformations represented by unitary matrices to diagonalize them. Their relative transformation appears in the charged weak current as the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix. The weak neutral currents remain diagonal in the minimal Standard Model, since the same-charge couplings are generation-independent. Three nondegenerate generations give three mixing angles and one physical weak CP phase after quantum field rephasings.

Transverse massless leptonic current (qμℓμ​=0)

Words: 49
Charged current OurBigBook.com
For two outgoing massless leptons, ℓμ​=uˉ(q1​)γμ​(1−γ5)v(q2​) is transverse to q=q1​+q2​. This follows from the massless Dirac equation and anticommutation of the chirality matrix with the gamma matrices. Thus the qμf−​(q2) term in a pseudoscalar-to-pseudoscalar form factor does not contribute to this scattering amplitude. A nonzero charged-lepton mass spoils exact transversality and restores a mass-suppressed scalar-form-factor contribution.

Weak flavour selection in neutrino-electron scattering

Words: 48
Charged current OurBigBook.com
The weak charged current pairs each neutrino with its corresponding charged lepton. Thus elastic muon-neutrino/electron scattering has only tree-level neutral-current exchange, while electron-neutrino and electron-antineutrino scattering also have crossed and annihilation charged-current diagrams. A contact term pairing a muon neutrino directly with an electron would violate this Standard Model flavour assignment.

Helicity suppression

Words: 46
Charged current OurBigBook.com
A spin-zero parent decaying through a chiral weak charged current to a charged lepton and a massless neutrino cannot supply the helicities selected by a massless interaction. A charged-lepton mass insertion makes the amplitude proportional to mℓ​ and the decay width proportional to mℓ2​. A spin-one W boson does not suffer this suppression.

For the massless contact interaction −(GF​/2​)[dˉγα(P+Qγ5)u][cˉγα​(P+Qγ5)s] with real P,Q, spin and colour averaging gives
dΩdσ​=128π2GF2​s​[(P2+Q2)2(1+cos2θ)+8P2Q2cosθ].
(1)
The gamma matrix trace identities give the averaged amplitude 4GF2​[(C2+4P2Q2)(p2​⋅k1​)(p1​⋅k2​)+(C2−4P2Q2)(p2​⋅k2​)(p1​⋅k1​)], where C=P2+Q2. Substitute the massless Mandelstam variables and divide by 64π2s. The two singlet colour contractions give factor one after final summation and initial averaging. This is a low-energy Fermi interaction result, not its high-energy extrapolation.
Neutrino scattering on an antiquark (dσuˉ​/dy=GF2​s(1−y)2/π)
Words: 33
Weak charged-current quark scattering OurBigBook.com
For a massless neutrino scattering on an unpolarized up antiquark through the Fermi interaction, dσ/dy=GF2​s(1−y)2/π. The corresponding down-quark channel has dσ/dy=GF2​s/π. Their difference follows from the chiral weak-current trace contraction. The parton distribution functions weight these rates in a hadron.
Chiral weak-current trace contraction (Tαβ(a,b)Tαβ​(c,d))
Words: 37
Weak charged-current quark scattering OurBigBook.com
For massless momenta, define Tαβ(a,b)=Tr[aγα(1−γ5)bγβ(1−γ5)]. The gamma matrix trace identities and the antisymmetric tensor contraction give Tαβ(a,b)Tαβ​(c,d)=256(a⋅c)(b⋅d). Reversing an antiquark's spinor order changes the momentum pairing and creates the (1−y)2 angular factor in a weak charged-current quark scattering rate.
Angular asymmetry of a chiral charged-current interaction (A(θ))

Weak charged-current quark scattering OurBigBook.com
For the massless common vector-axial coupling at both vertices in weak charged-current quark scattering, subtracting opposite directions gives
A(θ)=(P2+Q2)28P2Q2​1+cos2θcosθ​.​
(2)

The inequality 4P2Q2≤(P2+Q2)2 implies ∣A∣≤1. This unpolarized observable does not distinguish purely left- from purely right-handed couplings applied at both vertices.

Neutral current

Words: 189 Articles: 4
Weak interaction OurBigBook.com
The weak neutral current couples the Z boson to a fermion without changing its electric charge. Its vector and axial-vector coefficients depend on weak isospin, electric charge, and the weak mixing angle.

Neutral-current vector and axial couplings (cV​=(gL​+gR​)/2,cA​=(gL​−gR​)/2)

Words: 49
Neutral current OurBigBook.com
If a neutral-current vertex has prefactor g/cosθW​ and chiral coefficients gL​,gR​, then gL​PL​+gR​PR​=cV​−cA​γ5, with cV​=(gL​+gR​)/2 and cA​=(gL​−gR​)/2. For one Standard Model charged lepton, (cV​,cA​)=(−1/4+sin2θW​,−1/4); for an active neutrino, (cV​,cA​)=(1/4,1/4). A prefactor g/(2cosθW​) instead requires doubled coefficients. Mixing these conventions creates a factor-of-four error in squared amplitudes.

Flavor-changing neutral current

Words: 110 Articles: 2
Neutral current OurBigBook.com
A flavor-changing neutral current changes fermion flavor without changing electric charge. Such currents are absent at tree level in the Standard Model and are strongly suppressed at loop level by the Glashow-Iliopoulos-Maiani mechanism.
GIM mechanism
Words: 47
Flavor-changing neutral current OurBigBook.com
Unitarity of the CKM matrix cancels flavour-independent contributions to weak flavour-changing neutral amplitudes. In a quark loop, equal internal masses would give a common contribution whose off-diagonal CKM sum vanishes; unequal masses leave a suppressed nonzero amplitude. This explains why neutral kaon mixing occurs through loops rather than a tree neutral-current vertex.
Glashow-Iliopoulos-Maiani mechanism (GIM mechanism)
Words: 31
Flavor-changing neutral current OurBigBook.com
The Glashow-Iliopoulos-Maiani mechanism uses the unitarity of the quark mixing matrix to cancel flavor-changing neutral-current amplitudes when equal-charge quark masses are degenerate. The remaining loop amplitudes are suppressed by quark-mass differences.

Accidental symmetry

Words: 30
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
An accidental symmetry is respected by every operator of the chosen field content and dimension even though it was not imposed when constructing the theory. Higher-dimensional operators can violate it.

Hierarchy problem

Words: 277 Articles: 5
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
The hierarchy problem asks why the Higgs mass remains far below a much larger ultraviolet scale when scalar mass parameters receive additive radiative corrections proportional to that scale squared.

Technical hierarchy problem

Words: 61
Hierarchy problem OurBigBook.com
The technical hierarchy problem asks why a small mass scale, once chosen, remains stable under quantum corrections from much larger scales. A symmetry can protect this radiative stability without explaining the numerical origin of the scale separation. For a fundamental scalar mass, heavy thresholds often give additive corrections proportional to the heavy mass squared; supersymmetric cancellation of quadratic divergences supplies one protection mechanism when supersymmetry breaking is sufficiently soft.

Naturalness (physics)

Words: 187 Articles: 3
Hierarchy problem OurBigBook.com
Naturalness is the expectation that a dimensionless observable should not be extremely small because unrelated large contributions cancel with high precision. It is a heuristic guide to model building rather than a mathematical consistency condition.

Symmetry protection of a small mass

Words: 152 Articles: 2
Naturalness (physics) OurBigBook.com
A small mass is technically protected when its vanishing restores a symmetry that restricts the corresponding quantum corrections. Gauge protection of a vector mass, chiral protection of a fermion mass, and supersymmetry protection of scalar masses use different symmetry constraints. This is a radiative-stability statement, not a proof that all small numerical parameters require such protection.
Chiral protection of a fermion mass
Words: 59
Symmetry protection of a small mass OurBigBook.com
A fermion mass that violates an otherwise restored chiral symmetry is multiplicatively rather than additively renormalized in perturbation theory: corrections vanish with the symmetry-breaking mass or coupling. A chiral gauge representation can forbid a bare mass altogether until a Higgs mechanism and Yukawa coupling make a gauge-invariant term possible. A scalar-partner bilinear may respect all those ordinary symmetries and therefore needs separate supersymmetry protection.
Gauge protection of a vector mass
Words: 48
Symmetry protection of a small mass OurBigBook.com
An unbroken gauge symmetry forbids an explicit local Proca mass for its gauge vector. A Higgs mechanism can generate that mass through a charged vacuum expectation value, but the stability of the resulting vector scale then depends on the scalar sector that fixes the expectation. Gauge invariance alone does not protect a fundamental scalar mass.

Quantum chromodynamics (QCD)

Words: 3k Articles: 79
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
Quantum chromodynamics is the SU(3)c​ gauge theory of quarks and gluons. At low energies it confines coloured fields into gauge-singlet hadrons.

Massless two-flavor QCD symmetries (SU(2)L​×SU(2)R​×U(1)V​)

Words: 60
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
The gauge-covariant kinetic term for two massless quarks separates into left- and right-handed parts. Independent constant unitary quark flavor rotations preserve these terms, giving classical U(2)L​×U(2)R​ internal symmetry in addition to local color SU(3). The singlet axial U(1)A​ has a chiral anomaly, while the nonsinglet chiral symmetry and vector baryon number remain exact quantum symmetries, up to their shared discrete identifications. Equal nonzero quark masses reduce the continuous flavor symmetry to SU(2)V​×U(1)V​.

Jet (particle physics)

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
A collimated collection of final hadrons associated with an energetic parton and its radiation and hadronization. A precise perturbative prediction requires an infrared-safe observable that specifies how particles are grouped into jets.

Three-jet event

Words: 35
Jet (particle physics) OurBigBook.com
In inclusive electron-positron annihilation into hadrons, hard gluon radiation produces a quark, an antiquark and a gluon, giving three resolved particle jets. Observation of such events at PETRA in 1979 provided direct evidence for gluons. The institutional account is www.desy.de/news/news_search/index_eng.html?openDirectAnchor=1643&printversion=1 .

Real-virtual infrared cancellation in inclusive QCD

Words: 63
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
For an infrared-safe observable, loop corrections and integrated unresolved real emissions have compensating infrared divergences and collinear divergences. Keep a common regulator until they are added. At the first QCD correction to photon-mediated quark production, virtual gluon exchange corrects the two-parton state and real emission supplies the three-parton state. Their inclusive sum is finite after ultraviolet renormalization; resolved three-jet rates additionally depend on an infrared-safe resolution prescription.

Hadronization

Words: 39
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
Hadronization is the conversion of colored quarks and gluons into color-neutral hadrons. It affects exclusive final-state distributions even when an inclusive observable can be approximated through a short-distance partonic calculation. A tree-level partonic decay width does not by itself model this conversion.

Quark-hadron duality

Words: 44
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
Quark-hadron duality is the correspondence, in suitable inclusive or averaged observables, between a quark-level description and a sum over hadronic states. Asymptotic freedom supports perturbative short-distance production, but sharp resonances and threshold regions can invalidate a pointwise partonic approximation. Inclusive predictions can have both radiative and nonperturbative corrections.

Large-Nc baryon scaling (MB​,Λ,Fπ2​,e−2=O(Nc​))

Words: 66
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
In the large-color limit of QCD with gs2​Nc​ fixed, baryon masses scale as Nc​ while meson masses remain of order one. A Skyrme model action with coefficients of order Nc​ has soliton mass and rotational moment of inertia of order Nc​, and rotor splittings of order 1/Nc​. This motivates a semiclassical mesonic description of baryons; it does not uniquely determine every term in a finite-color effective theory.

Strong coupling constant (αs​=gs2​/(4π))

Words: 24
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
The strong coupling constant parametrizes the strength of Quantum chromodynamics interactions. Its dependence on the renormalization scale is governed by the renormalization-group beta function. It is dimensionless in four dimensions.

Color charge

Words: 122 Articles: 2
Quantum chromodynamics OurBigBook.com
Color charge is the gauge group charge of Quantum chromodynamics, associated with its SU(3) symmetry. A quark transforms in the fundamental three-dimensional representation, an antiquark in its conjugate, and a lepton is a singlet. The word color is a label for this charge, unrelated to visible light.

Colour singlet

Words: 36
Color charge OurBigBook.com
A colour singlet transforms in the trivial representation of the SU(3) colour group. Global colour rotations leave it invariant, and its colour generators annihilate it. A three-quark colour singlet uses the completely antisymmetric colour tensor; a quark–antiquark singlet contracts their colour indices.

Color multiplicity in a decay width (Nc​=3)

Words: 45
Color charge OurBigBook.com
For a colorless parent decaying through a color-diagonal interaction into a quark and antiquark, the three orthogonal matching-color states add incoherently. The inclusive flavor decay width is Nc​=3 times the one-color width. In a parton scattering rate, an initial color average instead cancels the matching final color sum.

Parton model

Words: 414 Articles: 9

For a negative muon with rest-frame spin vector s, the leading massless-electron distribution is dΓ/(dxdΩ)=GF2​mμ5​x2[(3−2x)+(1−2x)k⋅s]/(384π4), where x=2Ee​/mμ​∈[0,1]. Its final-spin sum is 64GF2​(k⋅q′)(q⋅(p−mμ​s)). The spin vector is axial whereas the electron direction is polar, so their scalar product reverses under parity. Its occurrence demonstrates parity violation by the left-chiral weak charged current.
Antimuon (μ+)
Words: 13
Muon OurBigBook.com
The antimuon is the antiparticle of the muon. It has electric charge +1 and lepton number −1.

Quark

Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com

Quark mass (Lm​=−∑f​mf​qˉ​f​qf​)

Words: 57
Quark OurBigBook.com
A quark mass is the coefficient of its Dirac mass term. This term couples left- and right-handed quarks, so nonzero quark masses explicitly break independent rotations of the two chiralities. For two equal masses, the vector flavor symmetry survives, while the nonsinglet axial current obeys the flavor-nonsinglet axial Ward identity with equal quark masses. In the renormalized theory the mass parameter depends on the subtraction scale and scheme, while measurable hadron masses are physical observables.

Quark field (ψi(x),i=1,2,3)

Words: 47
Quark OurBigBook.com
A quark field is a Dirac field or a chiral Weyl spinor carrying the colour fundamental representation of SU(3). Its three colour components transform as ψi↦Uij​ψj under local gauge transformations. The colour index is independent of the Lorentz spinor index, and the weak representations of its left and right chiral components differ in the Standard Model.

Quark flavor (u,d,s,c,b,t)

Words: 61
Quark OurBigBook.com
A quark flavor is one of the six Standard Model quark species: up, down, strange, charm, bottom and top. Each flavor occurs in three colour states and is counted as one Dirac species when both chiralities are included. The active flavor number in a low-energy QCD description excludes quarks heavier than the relevant scale, with matching of the running coupling when a heavy threshold is crossed.

Top quark (t)

Words: 40
Quark OurBigBook.com
The top quark is the up-type member of the third quark generation. Its mass exceeds the W boson mass, so a real W boson cannot decay into an on-shell top quark. A massless approximation for accessible decay products must not silently remove this channel threshold.

Spectator quark

Words: 24
Quark OurBigBook.com
A constituent quark that does not participate in the elementary weak vertex of a meson decay. It combines with a produced quark or antiquark in the final hadron.

Standard Model representation

Words: 129 Articles: 2
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
The Standard Model representations under SU(3)C​×SU(2)L​×U(1)Y​ are QL​=(3,2)1/6​, uR​=(3,1)2/3​, dR​=(3,1)−1/3​, LL​=(1,2)−1/2​, eR​=(1,1)−1​, and H=(1,2)1/2​.

Quark doublet (QL​=(uL​,dL​)T∼(3,2)1/6​)

Words: 51
Standard Model representation OurBigBook.com
In one Standard Model generation, the left-handed up and down quark fields form a weak SU(2) doublet of hypercharge 1/6. Each weak component has three colours. The same field therefore counts as three doublets for weak gauge-loop contributions and two colour fundamentals for strong gauge-loop contributions. Right-handed up and down quarks are separate weak singlets.

Electroweak representation and hypercharge table (Q=T3​+Y)

Words: 56
Standard Model representation OurBigBook.com
In normalization Q=T3​+Y, the left quark doublet has Y=1/6, right up/down singlets have 2/3,−1/3, the left lepton doublet has −1/2, the right charged lepton has −1, and the Higgs doublet has 1/2. The alternative convention Q=T3​+Y/2 uses Y=2Y. Up-type Yukawa interactions use the conjugate doublet of hypercharge −1/2.

Baryon number (B)

Words: 115 Articles: 3
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
Baryon number assigns B=1/3 to each quark, B=−1/3 to each antiquark and zero to leptons. A proton has baryon number one.

Baryon plus lepton number (B+L)

Words: 34
Baryon number OurBigBook.com
Baryon plus lepton number is the sum of baryon number and lepton number. It is an accidental classical symmetry of the renormalizable Standard Model but has an SU(2)L​ chiral anomaly, so electroweak instantons and sphalerons violate it.

Proton decay

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Baryon number OurBigBook.com
Proton decay is a hypothetical baryon-number-violating transition of the proton into lighter particles. Its nonobservation places strong lower bounds on the scale, or strong upper bounds on the couplings, of baryon-number-violating interactions.
Proton-decay operator
Words: 28
Proton decay OurBigBook.com
A proton-decay operator is a local effective interaction that violates baryon number. Standard Model gauge invariance first permits such operators at dimension six, including QQQL and ucucdcec.

Lepton number (L)

Words: 165 Articles: 5
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
Lepton number assigns L=1 to leptons, L=−1 to antileptons and zero to quarks. Neutrino masses show that separate family lepton numbers need not be exact.

Neutrino

Words: 140 Articles: 4
Lepton number OurBigBook.com
A neutrino is an electrically neutral spin-one-half lepton. The Standard Model has three active neutrino flavours associated with the electron, muon and tau.
Mixing of exactly massless neutrinos is removable
Words: 55
Neutrino OurBigBook.com
If all neutrinos are exactly massless, arbitrary unitary rotations among them preserve both their kinetic terms and their zero mass matrix. After diagonalizing the charged-lepton Yukawa matrix, choose the neutrino basis to coincide with that rotation. The resulting weak charged current has no physical lepton mixing matrix. With nondegenerate neutrino masses this extra basis freedom is lost, permitting observable neutrino oscillations and lepton mixing.
Muon neutrino (νμ​)
Words: 22
Neutrino OurBigBook.com
The muon neutrino is the neutral lepton coupled to a muon by the weak charged current. It carries lepton number +1; its antineutrino has the opposite lepton number.
Antineutrino
Words: 15
Neutrino OurBigBook.com
An antineutrino is the antiparticle of a neutrino and carries the opposite additive lepton number.
Neutrino oscillation
Words: 25
Neutrino OurBigBook.com
Neutrino oscillation is the coherent conversion between neutrino flavors caused by different propagation phases of mixed mass eigenstates. It measures mass-squared differences and mixing parameters.

Right-handed neutrino

Words: 248 Articles: 5
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
A right-handed neutrino transforms as (1,1)0​ under SU(3)c​×SU(2)L​×U(1)Y​, so it is neutral under every Standard Model gauge interaction.

Gauge-invariant right-handed neutrino Majorana mass (−21​MνRc​​νR​+Hermitian conjugate)

Words: 66
Right-handed neutrino OurBigBook.com
A right-handed neutrino is a singlet of the entire Standard Model gauge group. Its same-chirality bilinear with the field obtained by charge conjugation therefore admits the displayed renormalizable Majorana mass term, in addition to a Higgs-induced Dirac mass term. It violates lepton number by two units. Analogous terms for electrically charged Standard Model fermions carry nonzero electric charge; quarks also have nontrivial color charge. The presence of a right-handed field permits mass but does not force a nonzero mass parameter.

Seesaw mechanism

Words: 161 Articles: 3
Right-handed neutrino OurBigBook.com
The type-I seesaw mechanism combines a Dirac neutrino mass mD​ with a much larger right-handed-neutrino Majorana mass term M. Diagonalizing the mass matrix gives a light eigenvalue of order mD2​/M and a heavy eigenvalue of order M.
Weinberg operator
Words: 102 Articles: 1
Seesaw mechanism OurBigBook.com
The Weinberg operator is the dimension-five Standard Model operator (LH)(LH)/Λ. After the Higgs field condenses, it gives a left-handed neutrino Majorana mass of order v2/Λ.
Majorana neutrino mass from the Weinberg operator (mν​=∣G∣v2)
Words: 77
Weinberg operator OurBigBook.com
For the gauge-singlet composite χ=ϕ​†L, the interaction GχTC−1χ−G∗χˉ​Cχˉ​T is electroweak gauge-invariant. At the Higgs field vacuum, χ=vνL​/2​, giving 21​(Gv2νLT​C−1νL​−G∗v2νˉL​CνˉLT​). The Grassmann variation of a chiral Majorana mass term therefore identifies the mass parameter as Gv2, with physical mass ∣G∣v2. The dimension-five interaction has a coupling of mass dimension minus one. Under lepton number phase rotation, its two terms acquire factors e±2iα, so it violates continuous lepton number by two units. It is an effective extension of the minimal renormalizable Standard Model.
Type-II seesaw mechanism
Words: 23
Seesaw mechanism OurBigBook.com
The type-II seesaw mechanism couples two lepton doublets to an electroweak scalar triplet. A small neutral-triplet vacuum expectation value directly generates a left-handed neutrino Majorana mass term.

Yukawa interaction

Words: 572 Articles: 9
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
A Yukawa interaction couples left- and right-handed fermions through a scalar field. Replacing the Higgs field by its vacuum expectation value turns a gauge-invariant Standard Model Yukawa interaction into a fermion mass term.

Yukawa scalar self-energy pole coefficients (τ2(1)​=−y2(4p2+24M2)/(ε16π2)+O(1))

Words: 41
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
For one four-component Dirac field with scalar interaction −yψˉ​ψϕ and the mostly-plus propagator convention, the fermion loop numerator is 4[M2−k⋅(k−p)]. Reduce it to a bubble and tadpole: −4y2[(2M2+p2/2)J−I]. Dimensional regularization gives pole parts J=2/(ε16π2) and I=−2M2/(ε16π2). The local pole then requires both wavefunction renormalization and a scalar mass counterterm.

Tree scattering in Yukawa theory (Lint​=−gψˉ​ϕψ)

Words: 170 Articles: 1
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
For a real scalar coupled through −gψˉ​ϕψ, the scalar-fermion Feynman vertex is −ig. Two-fermion scattering has scalar exchange in the t and u channels with a relative minus from exchanging identical external fermions. Fermion-antifermion scattering has t exchange and s annihilation, again with a relative fermionic minus for a fixed state ordering. Fermion-scalar scattering has the two orderings along one open fermion line, using internal momenta p1​+p2​ and p1​−p4​; these have the same sign. The Mandelstam variables specify the propagator denominators.
Tree scattering with pseudoscalar exchange (V=−igγ5)
Words: 90
Tree scattering in Yukawa theory OurBigBook.com
The pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction with coefficient −g has the displayed Feynman vertex. Its two-fermion tree-level Feynman diagrams are the t and u exchanges; antisymmetry of the final identical fermions requires their relative minus. Fermion-antifermion scattering has t exchange and s annihilation, again with a relative minus. With initial and final states ordered as b1†​d2†​∣0⟩ and b3†​d4†​∣0⟩, the normal-ordered current contributes −d†dvˉγ5v in the exchange channel but db and b†d† in the annihilation channel. These fermionic signs fix the overall sign as well as their interference; changing an external-state phase changes both terms together.

Gauge-invariant electron Yukawa mass (me​=∣ye​∣v/2​)

Words: 49
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
The Standard Model lepton doublet L=(νL​,eL​)T has hypercharge −1/2, the electron singlet eR​ has −1, and the Higgs doublet has 1/2. Therefore −ye​LˉϕeR​+h.c. is gauge-invariant even though a bare eˉL​eR​ mass is not. The vacuum expectation value generates a Dirac mass ∣ye​∣v/2​. In unitary gauge, the Higgs boson coupling is −(me​/v)heˉe after rephasing the electron.

Pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction (igψˉ​γ5ψϕ)

Words: 155 Articles: 1
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
A pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction couples a Dirac field bilinear containing the chirality matrix to a spin-zero field. In the standard mostly-minus gamma matrix convention with γ5=iγ0γ1γ2γ3 and the usual Dirac adjoint, igψˉ​γ5ψϕ is Hermitian for real g and real ϕ. If ϕ is a pseudoscalar, the interaction also preserves parity symmetry in quantum field theory; if ϕ is parity even, it breaks that symmetry. Moving the factor i into the definition of γ5 changes the displayed vertex coefficient but not the interaction. Each vertex has one bosonic leg and two oppositely oriented fermion legs, and preserves Dirac fermion number conservation.
Hermiticity of a pseudoscalar Dirac bilinear ((ψˉ​γ5ψ)†=−ψˉ​γ5ψ)
Words: 71
Pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
With the usual Dirac adjoint, Hermitian γ5 and {γ0,γ5}=0, taking the adjoint gives ψ†γ5γ0ψ=−ψ†γ0γ5ψ. Consequently a real pseudoscalar with coupling −gϕψˉ​γ5ψ has a Hermitian interaction only if g∗=−g. Writing g=igP​ with real gP​ gives the familiar interaction −igP​ϕψˉ​γ5ψ. Formal Euler-Lagrange field equations obtained with independent spinor and adjoint variables can still be computed for the original symbolic coupling; it must not silently be identified with a real physical coupling.

Fermion mass matrix (−fˉ​L​Mf​fR​+h.c.)

Words: 39
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
After a scalar vacuum expectation value, a Yukawa matrix produces a bilinear −fˉ​L​Mf​fR​+h.c.. Independent unitary left/right rotations diagonalize Mf​ with nonnegative masses. Extra scalar-dependent operators can make the physical scalar coupling matrix fail to diagonalize with the mass matrix.

Yukawa matrix (Yf​)

Words: 85 Articles: 1
Yukawa interaction OurBigBook.com
A Yukawa matrix contains the flavor-space couplings between left-handed fermions, right-handed fermions, and a scalar field. Its singular values determine fermion masses after symmetry breaking, while mismatches between its diagonalizing transformations produce flavor mixing.
Charged-lepton Yukawa matrix diagonalization (UL†​Yℓ​UR​=diag(ye​,yμ​,yτ​))
Words: 51
Yukawa matrix OurBigBook.com
A singular value decomposition of the charged-lepton Yukawa matrix uses independent unitary rotations of left- and right-handed leptons. Their gauge-covariant kinetic terms are unchanged because each rotation mixes identical Standard Model representations. After electroweak symmetry breaking, the nonnegative singular values give Dirac masses mi​=yi​v/2​ and diagonal Higgs boson couplings mi​/v. When the neutrinos are massless, rotating their left-handed fields with the charged partners preserves the diagonal weak charged current.

Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix (VCKM​)

Words: 414 Articles: 8
Standard Model fermion OurBigBook.com
The Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix is the unitary mismatch between the left-handed transformations that diagonalize the up- and down-quark Yukawa matrices. It appears in charged weak currents.

CKM unitarity triangle (Vud​Vub∗​+Vcd​Vcb∗​+Vtd​Vtb∗​=0)

Words: 52
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
Orthogonality of two CKM rows or columns makes the three complex products form a closed triangle. Its area is ∣J∣/2, where J is the Jarlskog invariant. Normalizing the displayed column-orthogonality relation gives vertices 0,1,ρˉ​+iηˉ​, with ρˉ​+iηˉ​=−Vud​Vub∗​/(Vcd​Vcb∗​). A collapsed triangle has zero weak rephasing-invariant CP violation for nondegenerate quark masses.

Wolfenstein parametrization (λ, A, ρ, η)

Words: 56
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
The Wolfenstein parametrization expands the three-generation CKM matrix in its small 1-2 mixing parameter λ=s12​, defining s23​=Aλ2 and s13​eiδ=Aλ3(ρ+iη). To cubic order its rows are (1−λ2/2,λ,Aλ3(ρ−iη)), (−λ,1−λ2/2,Aλ2), and (Aλ3(1−ρ−iη),−Aλ2,1). Higher orders restore exact unitarity. Rephasing-invariant barred parameters are defined from ratios of CKM entries rather than this truncated expansion.

Quark rephasing and CP conservation

Words: 156 Articles: 1
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
For nondegenerate quark masses, independent phase changes of the up- and down-quark mass eigenfields alter the numerical CKM matrix by row and column phases without changing physics. Thus CP symmetry requires that some allowed phase convention makes the matrix real, rather than requiring real entries in every convention. With N generic families, removing 2N−1 phases from a unitary matrix leaves (N−1)(N−2)/2 physical CP-violating phases and N(N−1)/2 mixing angles.
CP transformation of a charged quark current (Lcc​(V)CP​Lcc​(V∗))
Words: 92
Quark rephasing and CP conservation OurBigBook.com
Under charge conjugation, uˉγμ(1−γ5)d becomes −dˉγμ(1+γ5)u. Parity reverses the chirality again and applies the Lorentz parity matrix. The minus sign cancels that of charge conjugation on the charged vector field. Thus each charged-current operator is exchanged with its Hermitian conjugate under CP symmetry, giving the displayed transformation for the CKM matrix V. For nondegenerate quark masses, physical CP conservation means that allowed quark rephasings can make V real. A nonzero Jarlskog invariant obstructs this. A merely complex phase convention is not proof of physical CP violation, and V=I is a CP-conserving counterexample to unconditional noninvariance.

CKM parameter counting ((N−1)2)

Words: 42
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
An N×N CKM matrix starts with N2 parameters of a unitary matrix. Independent quark rephasings remove 2N−1 phases because the common phase has no effect. The remaining (N−1)2 parameters consist of N(N−1)/2 angles and (N−1)(N−2)/2 CP-violating phases. Extra mass degeneracies may reduce this generic count.

Cabibbo angle (θC​)

Words: 50 Articles: 1
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
The angle of the real two-generation quark mixing rotation, with Vud​=Vcs​=cosθC​, Vus​=sinθC​, and Vcd​=−sinθC​.
Cabibbo suppression
Words: 34
Cabibbo angle OurBigBook.com
A small weak charged current amplitude factor associated with sinθC​. A doubly suppressed amplitude contains two such factors, giving a rate suppression of order tan4θC​ relative to a favoured process when other matrix elements are comparable.

Jarlskog invariant (J)

Words: 33
Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix OurBigBook.com
The Jarlskog invariant is a rephasing-invariant measure of CP violation in a three-generation quark mixing matrix. It is the common magnitude of imaginary quartic products such as Im(Vij​Vkℓ​Viℓ∗​Vkj∗​) for distinct rows and columns.
